question.text: Kaveri Macro Fund (Cat III determinate trust) receives INR 50 lakh of dividend from Indian listed companies. The Fund is the representative assessee for a single individual-HUF beneficiary. Using the workbook's effective rate of 35.88% for individuals/HUF/AOP/BOI on dividend income (post deduction), the tax payable (ignoring the 20% interest-expense deduction) is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook table on dividend income, resident individuals/HUF/AOP/BOI face an effective rate of 35.88%. Tax = 50,00,000 × 35.88% = INR 17,94,000. The 20% interest-expense cap under Section 57 would only reduce this if the fund borrowed to fund the investment. The Trap: INR 21.37 lakh uses 42.744% MMR (that is interest rate, not dividend). INR 15 lakh uses flat 30%. INR 10 lakh uses 20% (non-resident rate under Section 115A). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D tests the same rate for Cat I/II pass-through LPs. XIX-B tests it from investor-communication. XIX-E places the burden on the fund (trustee as representative assessee) to withhold/pay at 35.88%. Manager's Pro-Tip: For high-dividend strategies at Kaveri, consider whether a debt-heavy capital structure makes sense — the 20% interest-expense deduction under Section 57 is narrow. Alternatively, prefer buyback / growth names where gain is LTCG (12.5%) rather than dividend (35.88% for individuals).
